1.16.7.en: * Job not only did not blaspheme, but even blessed! He was not content to bear his calamity in silence, but glorified God, not only at that time but for the future as well.

1.16.8.en: * If we practice this spiritual wisdom (constant thanksgiving), we will experience no evil, even if we fall under countless sufferings, but the gain will be greater than the loss, and good will overcome evil. By these words you make God merciful toward you, and He defends you against the tyranny of the devil. As soon as your tongue utters these words, Satan flees quickly from you.

1.16.9.en: * While (Job) was completely surrounded by that wealth, it was not apparent to many what kind of man he was. But when his garments were stripped from him like a wrestler's and he cast them aside, and came naked to the contests for the sake of godliness, he amazed all who saw him. Even the theater of the angels cried out when they beheld his soul steadfast in endurance, and they praised him as having won the crown. And as I noted before, men did not see him as well when he was wrapped in all the wealth as they saw him when he threw it off like a garment, and appeared as one naked on the stage in the midst of the world, and all were amazed at the strength of his soul. They bore witness to him not because he was stripped of everything, but because in his struggle he patiently bore his weaknesses.

1.16.10.en: * "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away" [21], to do what seems good to the Lord. See, he believed that it was God who took away... What can be compared with this attitude? He did not ask to know out of curiosity, and did not say: Why does God give to me? And why does He take?

1.16.11.en: "Blessed be the name of the LORD" [21]. Notice by what means he enjoys consolation...

1.16.12.en: It is the Lord who decided. You say: Why did God decide in this way...? When He made me rich I did not seek to know why He gave me wealth, and now I do not want to know why He took it from me. For did He give me this because of merit on my part? Did He give me this in return for good works?

1.16.13.en: He decided to give to me, and He did so. He decided to take, and He is doing this.

1.16.14.en: It is a sign of a godly spirit to do everything according to the will of God, and not to ask Him for an account, nor an explanation of what He does.

1.16.15.en: * It is a great thing if we are able to give thanks with great joy. But giving thanks out of fear is one thing, and giving thanks during grief is another. This is what Job did when he thanked God... Let no one say that he did not grieve over what befell him or that he was not affected by it in the depths. Do not take away from him the great praise of his righteousness... Satan harms us not in order to take away what is ours and leave us destitute, but because when this happens we are bound to blaspheme God.

1.16.16.en: * Job was crowned and became famous, not because he was not shaken despite the countless trials that surrounded him, and despite the opposition of his wife toward him, but because he continued in his thanks to the Lord in every state: not only when he was rich, but also when he became poor; not only when he was in health, but also when his body was struck (with sores); not when these things came upon him slowly, but when a violent storm came upon him, upon his house and also upon his whole person.

1.16.17.en: * Satan causes us losses, not only to take away our goods, for he knows that these are nothing, but to compel us by this to utter blasphemy. So in the case of blessed Job he did not strive only to make him poor but also to make him a blasphemer.

1.16.18.en: St. John Chrysostom * Although he was counted as the owner of great wealth, the test presented to him by the Lord showed clearly that he possessed nothing but God alone.

1.16.19.en: St. Macarius the Great * Praise the Lord on the harp. If you have an abundance of earthly things, give thanks to the Giver. If there is want or you are robbed of what is yours, play the harp with joy. For you have not been deprived of the Giver, even if you have been deprived of the gift He gave you. So I repeat, play with gladness. With full trust in your God, take hold of the strings of your hearts as of a harp, that your voices may resound to their depths, crying out: "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away."

1.16.20.en: * Here we find an example of a man who blesses the Lord at all times.

1.16.21.en: * Let Him take what He has given, but have you lost the Giver...? It is as though he says: Let Him take all, let Him take everything, and let Him send me away naked, but let me keep Him Himself. What do I lack if I possess God? Or what use is everything to me if I do not possess God?

1.16.22.en: *He could have said: "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away. What the Lord has taken He can give again, and restore more than He took." But he did not say this; he said: [What seems good to the Lord, let it be]. For what pleases Him pleases me. May what pleases the good Lord not grieve the submissive servant, as what pleases the physician does not grieve the patient.

1.16.23.en: * From where did such jewels of praise of God come? See a man who was poor outwardly, but inwardly was rich. Could such jewels have come from his lips if he had not carried a hidden treasure in his heart?

1.16.24.en: * O the inward wealth which no thief can approach! God gave him Himself. He enriched him when He offered Himself to him, in what he loves.

1.16.25.en: * You take what I have, you do not take what is within me. For he will not become poor who says: [The LORD gave, the LORD hath taken away; as it hath pleased in his eyes, so let it be; blessed be the name of the LORD].

1.16.26.en: * The mammon of unrighteousness is all the wealth of this world, whatever its source. When the rich man gathers, he is gathering the mammon of unrighteousness, that is, wealth of injustice... If we want true wealth, it is different from this wealth. This wealth was in abundance, yet when Job was naked his heart was full of divine things, overflowing with praises like the most precious jewels offered to his God, and that when he had lost all that he had.

1.16.27.en: * When you hear this, direct your hearts toward God. Do not deceive your souls.

1.16.28.en: Seek yourselves... whether you love the world or do not love it, and learn to let it depart before you depart. What does it mean that you let it depart? That is, do not let your hearts cling to it.

1.16.29.en: When you have something that you will one day lose, whether in life or by death, let it go, for it will not be able to accompany you forever.

1.16.30.en: Be prepared for the will of God and cling to Him. Hold fast to Him, whom you cannot lose without your own will. If an occasion arises for the loss of temporal things, say: "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away."

1.16.31.en: * Job was found worshipping God for God's own sake, loving Him for Himself, and not because He gave him what he needed, but because God Himself had not been taken from him... The fires of temptation approached him, but found him gold and not straw. They removed the dross from him, and did not turn him to ashes!

1.16.32.en: * If you have sinned, grieve over the loss of your inward treasure. You have nothing in your house, but your heart may be emptier still. But if your heart is full of His goodness, full of your God, why do you not say: "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; as it pleases the Lord, so let it be! Blessed be the name of the LORD!" What grieves God? Is it from the blows, when He Himself has been struck? Far be it!

1.16.33.en: * O the jewels of praise to God, which he brought out from his inward treasures! This is his wealth! He brought forth a sweet hymn that glorifies God and commends Job.

1.16.34.en: * What a courageous, sweet voice! Who does not awake from sleep at this voice? Who does not trust in God in wakefulness, to walk into the battle without fear against the devil, fighting not by his own strength but by the strength of the One who proves him?

1.16.35.en: St. Augustine * How shall I be fit to be in the company of Job, I who do not accept ordinary trials with thanksgiving?

1.16.36.en: * It is clear that the virtues become our possessions when they are practically woven into our nature. They do not leave us while we strive on this earth, unless we ourselves drive them away by our will and compel them to go, by opening the door for vice to enter.

1.16.37.en: They run with us eagerly whenever we hasten toward the other world.

1.16.38.en: They set those who possess them in the rank of the angels, and shine eternally in the eyes of the Creator.

1.16.39.en: But wealth and power and pleasure and the whole throng of such follies, which increase daily because of our folly, do not enter this life with us and do not accompany anyone when he leaves this world. For the saying of the righteous man of old: "Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither" (Job 1:21) is a saying truly established and prevailing for every man.

1.16.40.en: * Among the men of old and the men of today it is supposed that each of them enjoyed a certain success, as each enjoys a certain virtue: Job received undefeated patience in the midst of affliction, Moses and David meekness, Samuel prophecy looking to the future, and Phinehas zeal (Num 25:7-8)... Peter and Paul zeal in preaching (Gal 7:2), and the sons of Zebedee magnificence of style, so they were called sons of thunder (Mk 17:3).

1.16.41.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * This was something like a cry from him: "I was called a father for a long time, since He who created me wanted me to be so. Now He has wanted in turn to remove from me the crown of offspring. I do not resist Him in what is His. What seems good in His eyes, let it be done. He is the Creator of my children, and I am an instrument. Why should I, the servant, surrender to useless grief and bitter complaint against a decision that I cannot avoid in vain?" With such words he threw Satan to the ground.

1.16.42.en: St. Basil the Great * Have you seen the arrows that the traitor shot?

1.16.43.en: The enemy himself was plundered, and was confused in vain. For Job was not affected at all by the events, listening to the reports of the evils falling upon him as though they belonged to someone else, while he was like a rock that repels the waves that dash against it.

1.16.44.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem *If anyone bears the Lord's dispensation with patience, and says when he loses something: [The LORD gave, the LORD hath taken away...], he receives a crown for his patience, which pleases God if he is righteous, and forgiveness if he is a sinner.

1.16.45.en: * The righteous man who suffers destruction (of material things) is rich and naked. St. Job was full of this wealth... He lost all those things that God had given him, but he possessed God Himself, the Giver.

1.16.46.en: Fr. Caesarius, Bishop of Arles * See how he concludes everything he rightly felt by blessing the Lord. By this the enemy experienced shame, and it was counted against him as punishment and defeat. For he himself, though created in blessing, rebelled against the Lord (c), while that one who is mortal utters a hymn of glory even while under His disciplines... With words of patience he praised God when he was struck. He shot many arrows into the breast of his adversary, and wounded him with injuries more bitter than those under which he himself had fallen. For through his trial he lost earthly things, and by bearing them humbly he doubled his heavenly blessings.

1.16.48.en: * Holy Scripture says: "For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out" (1 Tim 6:7). Those who desire to be rich fall into many foolish and hurtful lusts. The disciple who became a traitor is a clear proof of this, for he perished for a little miserable money.

1.16.49.en: St. Cyril the Great * We are masters of ourselves; it is for us to harm ourselves or not to harm ourselves... (If all our treasures are stolen) it is truly a sad matter, and it seems a loss. But the matter remains dependent on you, for you can make it a loss or a gain for you. You say: "And how can this be a gain?" I am trying to show you how, for if you wish it will be a great gain for you, and if you do not wish, the loss will be harsher than the loss of what was taken from you. For as in the case of artists, when raw materials are placed before them, the one who is skilled in his art uses the materials for a good purpose, but the unskilled one spoils the materials and they become a loss for him. So it is here: how does this become a gain? If you give thanks to God, if you do not lament bitterly, if you utter the words of Job: "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away..."

1.16.50.en: * Who can calmly bear to see his only child laid out as a lifeless corpse? He needs a soul like steel to bear that. Such a one must rest from the sighs of nature, and be strengthened to utter the words of Job: [The LORD gave, the LORD hath taken away] (Job 21:1). By these words alone he stands with Abraham himself and Job to be proclaimed a victor. And if he forbids the wailing of women and disperses the groups of mourners to set them up to sing the glory of God, he receives above all countless rewards; men are astonished at him, the angels praise him, and God crowns him.

1.16.51.en: * These are the words of a living soul, a soul that performs the role fitting for it.

1.16.52.en: * Suppose that someone lost his son, and another all his possessions... Fruit can be gained from the affliction even if it cannot be remedied, by bearing the circumstances nobly, and instead of using words of blasphemy, offering words of thanks to the Lord; by this the evils that are brought upon you against your will become good works by your choice.

1.16.53.en: St. John Chrysostom * God is good, and all that He does must be good also.

1.16.54.en: Has He decided that I must lose my husband? Mourn my loss, but since this is His will, bear it with submission.

1.16.55.en: Is my only son snatched from me? A harsh blow, but it can be borne, because the One who takes is the same One who gave.

1.16.56.en: If I become blind, my friend's reading comforts me.

1.16.57.en: If I become deaf, I escape hearing evil words, and my thoughts are centered on God alone.

1.17.0.en: St. Jerome "In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly" [22].

1.17.1.en: This is a living testimony that the Holy Spirit gives us of his good conduct in the midst of affliction. He passed through the trial with success and true victory.

1.17.2.en: St. John Chrysostom sees in the expression "nor charged God foolishly" that he did not accuse God of injustice, nor did he reckon that what befell him was the product of chance, nor did he murmur, saying that he had not sinned, so why did evils come upon him, does God not care about him. Such thoughts come to some when trials come upon them while they see others enjoying temporal blessings.

1.17.3.en: * Satan fought (Job) steadfastly, but he was unable to win against the wrestler of God.

1.17.4.en: He emptied his quiver of arrows, but he was not able to wound his brave, valiant fighter.

1.17.5.en: He stirred up huge waves, but he could not move the firm rock.

1.17.6.en: He used his tricks, but he could not demolish the strong tower.

1.17.7.en: He shook the tree, but he did not shatter the fruit.

1.17.8.en: He broke the branches, but he did not harm the root.

1.17.9.en: He pierced the wall, but he did not carry off the treasure.

1.17.10.en: Now I say that this treasure to which I refer is not of gold or silver, but the faith of the righteous man. For Satan wanted to destroy this treasure when he stirred up against him an unbearable affliction after taking away all his wealth... You see God glorified and Satan put to shame.

1.17.11.en: Fr. Caesarius, Bishop of Arles * Satan and his angels failed to triumph over Job when they launched their attacks on him. He was the man who stands bold, who will not be shaken in his firm faith.

1.17.12.en: St. Augustine * Notice how Job is described as having come to a greater state through the temptation, while David fell to the ground by temptation. Therefore the virtues of our forebears may strengthen our hope, and their falls support our caution through humility, so that while by the former we are lifted up to joy, by the latter we remain in fear.

1.17.13.en: * "In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly" [22]... Since he uttered nothing in which there was folly, guarding his tongue from iniquity, while it is said "sinned not," it appears that he removed from himself the sin of murmuring even from his thought, so he did not sin, nor speak foolishly, nor did resentment rise in his silent feeling, nor did his tongue loose itself in cursing.

1.17.15.en: * Give thanks to God and praise the One who tests you in the furnace. Utter praise instead of blasphemy; this is the way in which that blessed man expressed himself.

1.17.16.en: * This is the way in which Job offered a sacrifice (of praise) although terrible sorrows beyond human strength had come upon him.

1.17.18.en: A hymn of praise in the midst of affliction!

1.17.19.en: * Grant me, O Lord, by Your grace, to enjoy spiritual wealth!

1.17.20.en: Let me be perfect in Your sight, You who charge Your angels with folly!

1.17.21.en: And count me upright, because of the work of Your Spirit in me!

1.17.22.en: Nail Your fear in my heart, that I may live in godliness.

1.17.23.en: And let Your light shine within me, that I may not bear to walk in the darkness of evil.

1.17.24.en: * Grant Your Church to be like the family of Job, her days feasts and spiritual banquets that never cease!

1.17.25.en: Her mark is brotherly love and agreement without division.

1.17.26.en: She plays the symphony of love that gladdens the heavenly beings!

1.17.27.en: In the midst of my joys, let the sacrifice of Your cross never depart from me!

1.17.28.en: I pray for my brethren as for my own lowliness, lest in ignorance or with knowledge I sin against You.

1.17.29.en: * Let the devil complain against me before You, for I take refuge under the shadow of Your wings!

1.17.30.en: There is none to support me but You!

1.17.31.en: * Let the devil strip me of everything!

1.17.32.en: But I possess You, and he will not draw me away from You.

1.17.33.en: You are my wealth and my happiness and my sufficiency in everything!

1.17.34.en: * In the midst of affliction my soul gives You thanks and praises You, for my heart is lifted up to You!

1.17.35.en: He has no place in the world, nor has the world any place in him!
